Add an overlay of channels

Source: R/add-overlay.R
add_overlay.Rd

Adds a panel that shows where channels coincide: a single-colour image that is bright only where all member channels are bright. It is computed as the minimum of the members' display-scaled intensities (0 to 1 within their display ranges), so it is "as bright as the weakest channel". Like a merge, an overlay is a new, virtual channel that can be placed in the layout like any other channel.

Usage

add_overlay(montage, ..., name = "overlay", color = "white", threshold = NULL)

Arguments

montage

A tidymontage() object.

...

Channels to merge, as bare names or strings. Use backticks or strings for names with spaces, e.g. `Alexa Fluor 488`.

name

Name of the overlay, as it appears in the layout and in labels.

color

Colour of the overlay. "black" shows it inverted, as dark signal on white. A colormap made with lut(), such as lut("inferno"), colours the overlay by its strength.

threshold

Optional threshold between 0 and 1 on the overlay intensity: pixels below it are shown as background. NULL (the default) shows the overlay as it is.

Value

The montage with the overlay step added.

Details

The overlay keeps the 0-1 scale it inherits and is not stretched again, so a faint overlap looks faint. Because it depends on the display ranges, keep them linked (the default of adjust_exposure()) when comparing conditions.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
montage |>
  add_overlay(GFP, Cy3, name = "overlap", color = "yellow")
} # }
